recognize_zh: 年長者手背皮膚薄且有日光損傷，上面有邊界不規則、深紫色的平坦瘀斑（ecchymosis），大於 1 公分且壓之不褪色，屬於皮下出血的臨床照片。
features: Irregular, flat, dark purple ecchymoses on the dorsum of the hand
Lesions larger than 1 cm with ill-defined edges, non-palpable
Thin, atrophic, sun-damaged skin of an older individual
No petechiae, palpable purpura or hemarthrosis evident in this view
describe_en: Clinical photograph shows the dorsal hand and wrist of an older adult with thin, photodamaged skin. There are irregular, confluent, flat violaceous ecchymoses over the dorsum of the hand, without visible petechiae or palpable lesions. The distribution on sun-exposed, easily traumatized skin is typical of senile (actinic) purpura, but ecchymoses can also reflect a coagulation factor deficiency, anticoagulant use or platelet dysfunction, so correlation with medication history, platelet count, PT and aPTT is required.

ddx.vs: Confined to sun-damaged forearms and hands of elderly patients with normal coagulation tests, as the distribution here suggests.
Presents with extensive spontaneous ecchymoses in the elderly but with an isolated prolonged aPTT and a factor VIII inhibitor.
Typically also shows petechiae and mucosal bleeding and is confirmed by platelet count or function testing.
Vasculitic lesions are raised, palpable and often on the lower legs, unlike these flat ecchymoses.
